name: Primary Cutaneous Aggressive Epidermotropic CD8+ T-cell Lymphoma
aliases: Aggressive Epidermotropic CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell Lymphoma
Primary Cutaneous CD8+ Cytotoxic T-cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of marked epidermotropism of atypical CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells on histopathology
Immunophenotyping showing CD8 positivity with cytotoxic markers (TIA-1, granzyme B, perforin) and absence of CD4
Rapidly progressive ulcerated or necrotic plaques or tumors primarily involving the skin without extracutaneous disease at diagnosis
Exclusion of other cutaneous T-cell lymphomas and systemic CD8+ lymphomas by clinical, histological, and molecular studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic epidermotropism with CD8+ cytotoxic immunophenotype and typical clinical presentation with exclusion of other lymphomas
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ulcerated necrotic cutaneous plaques or tumors
searchTerms: skin ulcers with dead tissue and sores
open necrotic skin plaques or tumors
ulcerated skin lesions with tissue death

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked epidermotropism of atypical CD8+ T-cells
searchTerms: skin infiltration by abnormal immune cells
atypical CD8+ T-cell accumulation in skin
unusual immune cell presence in skin

common.symptomName: Rapid lesion progression over weeks to months
searchTerms: skin lesions growing quickly over weeks

occasional.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating

occasional.notes: Due to necrosis and secondary infection
Rare but possible in advanced disease

rare.notes: Occurs in late or aggressive stages
searchTerms: spread of disease beyond skin to brain or lungs
cancer or infection involving CNS and lungs

laboratory: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD8, TIA-1, granzyme B, perforin
imaging: PET-CT or CT scan to exclude extracutaneous involvement
genetic: T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating clonality
No specific recurrent chromosomal translocations identified
other: Rapidly progressive clinical course with poor response to conventional therapies

redFlags: Failure to respond to standard cutaneous lymphoma therapies
Development of systemic symptoms or extracutaneous spread
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.

Bekkenk MW, Geelen FA, van Voorst Vader PC, et al. Primary and secondary cutaneous CD8+ T-cell lymphomas: a clinicopathologic, immunophenotypic, and molecular biologic study of 47 cases. Blood. 2003;102(3):781-789.
Sanchez-Espiridion B, Medeiros LJ, Wang SA, et al. Primary cutaneous aggressive epidermotropic CD8+ T-cell lymphoma: a clinicopathologic study of 10 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2008;32(8):1230-1239.
